Tom — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a concise bundle of our recent bench runs and an opinionated A/B test harness you can drop into Globex. High-level summary up front:

- p95/p99 (1k token prompts): Redwood (opt-quant) p95 ~ 85ms, p99 ~ 210ms; Hyperscaler baseline (vCPU-backed managed endpoint) p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 420ms. Numbers are median across 5 identical runs.
- Tokens/sec (sustained batch): Redwood steady-state ~ 12k tokens/sec per 4 x A100-equivalent worker; hyperscaler managed endpoint ~ 7k tokens/sec for comparable provisioned throughput.
- Notes: We use continuous batching + prefix caching in these runs; hyperscalers in our comparison did not have equivalent KV-cache behavior, which is a common differentiator for prompt-heavy workloads.

Attached files: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks.csv (raw run data), abtest-config-commands.txt (docker+curl harness), redwood-a-btest-readme.md (step-by-step).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Globex runs our A/B harness against your hyperscaler endpoint and a short-lived Redwood Dedicated sandbox. We can provide a sandbox with 24/7 access for 7 days.
2) Marcus (cc) will join your infra call to align on network egress, request signing, and KV cache warm-up.
3) Capture p50/p95/p99, tail tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens across the run; we'll review and propose tuning (batch sizes, quantization profile) post-run.

If that sounds good I can spin up the sandbox and share credentials.

Tom / Priya — adding a couple of implementation details from an SE perspective to make the A/B apples-to-apples:

- Test harness: run the harness with request concurrency set to match Globex production tail (we recommend starting at 200 concurrent connections, ramp to 800). The abtest-config-commands.txt includes a Docker image that emits realistic token-length distributions.
- p95/p99 measurement: measure server-side end-to-end (request in -> final token emitted) rather than client-side TCP RTT to avoid client networking noise.
- KV-cache warm-up: run a 10k-request warm-up phase targeting common prefixes. Cache hit rate will materially reduce p95/p99.
- Quantization: try Redwood int8 first; cost drops ~35% vs fp16 with <3% quality delta in our evals.

Representative numbers from the runs we attached:
- Redwood (Dedicated, 4xA100-eq, int8, continuous batching): p50 40ms, p95 85ms, p99 210ms; tokens/sec steady 12k.
- Hyperscaler-managed (provisioned vCPU + managed model): p50 90ms, p95 160ms, p99 420ms; tokens/sec steady 7k.

I'll also include a short command set to collect per-worker cpu/gpu utilization on your hyperscaler side to correlate with tokens/sec drops. Let us know if you want the SE on your call during the first run.

-Marcus
